rows.grounds: present passive participle of root chid, describing one undergoing cutting
optative passive form of root chid expressing potential or counterfactual cutting
compound of tad and gata indicating one who has reached that state
compound of tad and manas indicating one whose mind is absorbed in that

items.question: What immunity from harm does absorption in that state confer upon one being cut?
premises: A person may be subjected to the act of being cut.
Absorption in that state is characterized by having gone to it and having the mind fixed on it.
Such absorption alters the effect of physical injury on the practitioner.
items.inference: One who has reached that state and whose mind is fixed on it is not truly cut even while being cut.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that' (tad) depends on the preceding context.
The force of yathā at the verse end may imply a comparison completed in a following verse or an illustrative sense.
items.plain_english: One who has gone to that and whose mind is fixed on that, even while being cut, is not cut.
